Please review the following manuscript. I've poured months of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

/bin/bash -c "ls -la /fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/runtime/pdf && ls -la .agents/skills/pdf && python3 -c 'import importlib.util; print({name: bool(importlib.util.find_spec(name)) for name in [\"pypdf\", \"pdfplumber\", \"fitz\", \"PIL\"]})'"

/bin/bash -c "ls /fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/utility/.runtime/ghostscript-9.55.0 && python3 - <<'PY'
import shutil
for c in ['gs', 'pdftoppm', 'pdftotext', 'mutool']:
    print(c, shutil.which(c))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('tmp/pdfs')
p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
r = PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES', len(r.pages))
print('METADATA', r.metadata)
for i, page in enumerate(r.pages):
    text = page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    (p / f'page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(text)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n' + (p / f'page-{i+1:02}.txt').read_text() for i in range(len(r.pages))))
print((p/'page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('tmp/pdfs')
for i in range(1, 12):
    for suffix in ['txt', 'png']:
        (p / f'page-{i:02}.{suffix}').unlink()
(p / 'manuscript.txt').unlink()
p.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary review files; the manuscript is unchanged.')
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses an important problem in visual recognition: maintaining worst-group performance under spurious correlations and distribution shifts. SGDRO offers a simple, model-agnostic combination of average-loss perturbations and group-robust updates, with useful pseudocode in Algorithm 1.

Waterbirds experiments include ERM, SAM, and GDRO across five random seeds. With the same strong regularization as GDRO, SGDRO improves worst-group accuracy from 86.5% to 87.2% and group-average accuracy from 90.4% to 90.6% (Table 1).

The curvature measurements provide evidence beyond accuracy. Compared with GDRO, SGDRO reduces both reported leading Hessian eigenvalues in every group; the largest aggregate eigenvalue decreases from 356.6 to 268.7 (Table 2). This supports a local flattening effect.

Evaluation extends to six DomainBed datasets using training-domain validation for model selection and three random seeds. SGDRO achieves 71.4% average accuracy versus 70.1% for GDRO and 70.9% for ERM, suggesting practical usefulness beyond the motivating dataset.
weaknesses: The claimed guarantees of flat minima and worst-group generalization are unsupported. For a fixed worst group, the Taylor expansion of the update in Eq. (3) requires that group's gradient and Hessian, with the total-loss gradient defining the perturbation. Section 3.1 instead writes total-loss quantities throughout while interpreting them as worst-group quantities. Correcting this notation would still leave no argument establishing the claimed guarantees: a perturbation that increases average loss need not capture worst-group sharpness, and lower measured Hessian eigenvalues do not establish generalization under distribution shift.

The experiments do not isolate the value of the method's distinguishing design choices. There is no comparison against computing the SAM perturbation from the group-weighted GDRO objective, nor an ablation of updating group weights using perturbed losses. Table 3 also omits SAM. Consequently, the evidence does not establish whether the proposed coupling improves upon a direct combination of the existing components or ordinary sharpness-aware training.

The Waterbirds results support a modest robustness gain, but the claimed improvement in the average/worst-group trade-off is overstated. Worst-group accuracy rises by 0.7 percentage points while weighted average accuracy falls from 93.8% to 93.1%, and both majority groups deteriorate relative to GDRO. Table 1 does not define its uncertainty notation or report uncertainty for the aggregate worst-group metric, limiting confidence in the size of the improvement.

Reproducibility is only partial despite the helpful pseudocode and references to standard protocols. The DomainBed perturbation-radius search space, minibatch group-loss estimation, and treatment of regularization when constructing perturbations are insufficiently specified. These omissions matter for a method whose central operation depends on gradient direction.

Language and notation problems are secondary, correctable concerns. The factors determining my weak-reject recommendation are the unverified benefit of the defining algorithmic choices and the gap between the central guarantees and the evidence. The simple implementation and measured improvements are worthwhile, but currently provide insufficient support for the claimed contribution.
